parameters.content:
## AI Classification: Direct API Call, Not a Convenience Node
Deliberately uses HTTP Request against OpenAI's Chat Completions endpoint directly, not n8n's built-in OpenAI node. This is the point, not a workaround - it proves the ability to work with an LLM API directly (request/response shape, auth headers, JSON parsing) rather than only through a pre-built wrapper. `response_format: json_object` forces a parseable response; the Code node still wraps parsing in try/catch and falls back to General/Routine if the model ever returns something unparseable, so a bad AI response degrades safely instead of breaking the workflow.

**Why keyword classification was dropped in favor of this:** the user explicitly wants this project to prove AI-API skill for the portfolio - this is the one project in the sprint built specifically to demonstrate that, not to be the fastest possible build.

## Intake
Airtable Form (view on Maintenance Requests) writes new records directly into the base - no separate sync step, since Airtable owns the form natively. The trigger polls for new records; Category/Urgency/Assigned Contractor/Status stay blank until this workflow fills them in, which is also what makes 'is this row already processed' unambiguous - a blank Status means not yet handled.

## Error Handling
HTTP Request: Classify with OpenAI now has onError: continueRegularOutput
plus retry (3x/3s) - previously it had neither, so a single OpenAI blip
would kill the whole request before it ever reached Code: Parse
Classification's existing try/catch fallback (which defaults to
General/Routine but could never actually run). Every other node here
retries 3x/3s. Airtable: Find Available Contractor still stops the
workflow on failure - a graceful "no contractor found, notify requester
only" path needs an IF branch added, not just a retry, so that gap is
left open rather than silently changed. Points Settings -> Error Workflow
at the shared handler for anything else.
